prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: a production atlas of circular illustrated tokens for Creation, an original elemental myth about making a vast living world. The reference is the APPROVED STYLE AND CONTINUITY anchor, not a sheet to copy unchanged. Paint new subjects in exactly that family: luminous opaque gouache, selective fine ink contours, strong simplified silhouettes readable at 64px; deep lapis interiors, jade and turquoise, burnt ochre, muted coral, warm ivory light, very narrow ivory-gold rims. Not glossy coins or flat generic pictograms. Each icon is a complete perfect CIRCLE with opaque painted interior and transparent empty space outside. Center each circle in its own equal grid cell, circle diameter 80 percent of the shorter cell side, generous empty gutters. Absolutely no letters, names, numbers, grid lines, labels, UI, watermark or cast shadows outside circles. No modern laboratory hardware, books, houses or buildings. Only the specified object inside each circle, with a simple dark ground or essential local context. Tiny details must not carry the meaning. Related states should differ in structure, not merely colour. Follow item order exactly, left to right, top to bottom. Exactly 20 circles in 5 columns and 4 rows. Landscape atlas. Exact cell subjects: CELL 1, Multicellular life: A simple rounded ribbon-shaped body is assembled from two visibly different sizes of connected cells, with one continuous outer contour and a hollow central passage. Distinguish: Integrated differentiated cellular body rather than a loose rosette, recognizable animal or leafy alga. CELL 2, Algae: A small rooted-looking but unattached cluster of jade and olive seaweed fronds grows from a rough submerged stone; broad translucent blades bend underwater. Distinguish: One low seaweed cluster with no woody stem, terrestrial leaves or animal tentacles. CELL 3, Soft-bodied animals: A translucent oval marine animal with a gently lobed edge rests beside a slender worm-like companion; both have soft continuous bodies without hard shells or jointed legs. Distinguish: Soft simple animal bodies, distinct from a streamlined swimmer, armored jointed limbs or attached polyps. CELL 4, Swimming animals: A streamlined small marine animal swims diagonally, propelled by broad side fins and a clearly flexed tail, with a simple head and no emphasized eye. Distinguish: Active fish-like swimmer entirely underwater, without surfacing breath, mammal flippers or passive soft body shapes. CELL 5, Eyes: A close view of a small marine animal's head gives one large dark eye a bright highlight, while a narrow shaft of light reaches the eye from above. Distinguish: Eye structure and incoming light dominate; no primate gaze or night-adapted pair of eyes. CELL 6, Shells: Two hard pale marine shells sit against deep jade water: one strong spiral and one ribbed fan shape, both visibly hollow at the opening. Distinguish: Separate hard shell structures without an enclosing rock impression, embryo or translucent film. CELL 7, Fossils: A split ochre stone slab reveals a sharply outlined spiral-shell impression and a small ribbed shell trace embedded in the rock. Distinguish: Shell evidence inside stone, not loose living shells or giant rounded track impressions. CELL 8, Kelp forest: Three tall ochre-jade kelp stems rise from dark submerged rocks, bearing long ribbon blades and a few round gas floats beneath a pale water surface. Distinguish: Tall underwater canopy of kelp with holdfasts and floats; no land trunks or highlighted juvenile swimmers. CELL 9, Coral: One small colony of pale coral polyps attaches to a submerged stone, each polyp an open cup with a short crown of tentacles. Distinguish: Soft animal polyps are prominent; no vast hard reef architecture or plant-like frond. CELL 10, Reef partnership: One enlarged coral polyp shows a pale translucent body containing several small jade-green cells; its tentacles remain spread above a rough attachment stone. Distinguish: Algal cells visibly within a recognizable coral animal, not merely near it or inside an unrelated cell. CELL 11, Coral reef: A compact underwater reef combines several sturdy branching and mound-shaped pale coral skeletons, with tiny living coral tips and deep blue gaps between the structures. Distinguish: Large built calcium-carbonate architecture rather than a close polyp, tall kelp or broad multiple-habitat map. CELL 12, Nursery waters: Three tiny jade juvenile swimmers shelter within a protective arch of large ochre kelp blades, their small bodies sharply silhouetted in a calm dark gap. Distinguish: Young animals visibly sheltered by much larger kelp, not a plain kelp stand or independent swimming group. CELL 13, Coastal mosaic: An oblique strip of hooked coast contains separate cool dark kelp coves and warmer pale coral shallows, divided by rocky headlands and connected by blue water. Distinguish: Multiple spatially separated marine habitats in one broad strip; Living coast adds tidal exchange and exposed shelf. CELL 14, Living coast: The hooked ochre coast holds a kelp cove, a separate coral shallows and a broad tidal shelf; one sweeping jade tidal current connects the habitats around the cape. Distinguish: Rich connected coast with visible exchange, not bare shore or whole planet; keep kelp and coral in distinct coves. CELL 15, Waves: Three broad jade ocean swells approach in diagonal succession, the nearest curling into a clear ivory breaking crest over dark water. Distinguish: Rhythmic moving crests dominate, without a droplet, Moon or high-low shore comparison. CELL 16, Shore plants: Small upright green shoots and flat primitive-looking leaflets occupy wet cracks just above a jade shoreline, with algae still visible below the waterline. Distinguish: Transitional wet-margin land growth, not fully submerged seaweed, a dense moss cushion or isolated underground roots. CELL 17, Soil: A compact cutaway of dark crumbly topsoil shows pale fine roots, decomposed leaf fragments and scattered mineral grains beneath a thin green surface. Distinguish: Organic crumb structure and roots distinguish living soil from raw mineral matter, sorted sediment and soaked plant layers. CELL 18, Windblown spores: Fine pale spore grains blow from a small open capsule on a slender green stalk, spreading into a broad tapering trail above low wet growth. Distinguish: Minute unwinged reproductive grains from a capsule; no seed bodies, wings or embryo stores. CELL 19, Moss: A dense low cushion of bright jade moss carries several fine upright stalks with tiny brown capsules, rooted against a wet dark stone. Distinguish: Soft leafy cushion and capsule stalks, not a flat microbial film or large divided fronds. CELL 20, Wetland: A shallow dark pool lies among low mossy hummocks and saturated ochre ground, with several small patches of standing water connected below the growth. Distinguish: Waterlogged low vegetation without sea waves, desert sand or tall dry grasses. Keep the common circle size and painted finish. Anatomical lineages matter: insects have six legs, birds feathered wings, bats membranous finger-supported wings. A depicted early cell is a symbolic magnified view, not a modern laboratory slide. The world is not Earth's recognizable map. People, if listed, have varied warm earth-brown complexions, simplified features and no modern objects. Never add people, plants or animals to a subject that predates them. Do not draw the subject names.
